# Tenancy

**Package** `telividb.tenancy.v1`

## Services

### `Organizations`

Manages organizations, the root of the tenancy tree.  Every destructive method here returns the resource it acted on rather than an empty message. That is the soft-delete form, and it is not a workaround for a house style: deletion tombstones the resource so queries exclude it immediately and compaction reclaims the bytes later, so the resource still exists and describing it is the truthful response. An empty return would also be a dead end — a method returning it can never gain a field without a breaking change to a shipped signature.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CreateOrganization` | `CreateOrganizationRequest` | `Organization` | Creates an organization and the collection backing it. |
| `GetOrganization` | `GetOrganizationRequest` | `Organization` | Retrieves a single organization. |
| `ListOrganizations` | `ListOrganizationsRequest` | `ListOrganizationsResponse` | Lists organizations visible to the caller. |
| `UpdateOrganization` | `UpdateOrganizationRequest` | `Organization` | Updates an organization. |
| `DeleteOrganization` | `DeleteOrganizationRequest` | `Organization` | Soft-deletes an organization, tombstoning every collection beneath it. Returns the tombstoned organization carrying `delete_time` and `expire_time`. Nothing is physically removed here: the tenant becomes invisible to queries at once, and the bytes are reclaimed at expiry. Until then the operation is reversible. |
| `UndeleteOrganization` | `UndeleteOrganizationRequest` | `Organization` | Restores a soft-deleted organization before it expires. This is the rollback that a long-running transaction could not provide: the delete committed atomically in metadata and the data was never touched, so restoring it is another metadata write rather than a replay. |

### `Spaces`

Manages spaces and their protection.

| Method | Request | Response | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CreateSpace` | `CreateSpaceRequest` | `Space` | Creates a space with a declared protection state. Protection is fixed at creation because it determines segment routing: an encrypted space writes into its own segments so unlocking decrypts a region rather than a row at a time. Changing it later is a rewrite, not a field update. |
| `GetSpace` | `GetSpaceRequest` | `Space` | Retrieves a single space. |
| `ListSpaces` | `ListSpacesRequest` | `ListSpacesResponse` | Lists the spaces of an organization that the caller can see. |
| `UnlockSpace` | `UnlockSpaceRequest` | `UnlockSpaceResponse` | Unlocks a key-wrapped space for the duration of a session. |
| `DeleteSpace` | `DeleteSpaceRequest` | `Space` | Soft-deletes a space and every conversation within it. |

## Messages

### `Organization`

The top of the tenancy tree, and the only container that never changes for anything beneath it.  That permanence is why it is the one container that appears in a resource name: a conversation moves freely between projects and spaces, so encoding those in its name would make every move a rename and break every stored reference to it. Moving between organizations is an export, not a move.  An organization is also the physical boundary. One organization is one collection, so purging a tenant never rewrites another tenant's segments.

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the organization. |
| `display_name` | `string` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | Human-readable name. |
| `project_count` | `int32` | 3 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Projects belonging to this organization. |
| `space_count` | `int32` | 4 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Spaces belonging to this organization. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 5 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the organization was created. |
| `update_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the organization was last modified. |
| `delete_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the organization was soft-deleted, or unset while it is live. Deletion is reversible until `expire_time`. Nothing is physically removed at delete: the tenant is tombstoned so queries exclude it immediately, and compaction reclaims the bytes later. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When a soft-deleted organization is purged and becomes unrecoverable. |
| `etag` | `string` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

### `Project`

A unit of work within an organization, and the unit at which access is granted.  A project is a *predicate*, not a collection. At the scale this is designed for — organizations holding hundreds of projects each — a collection per project would mean thousands of manifests and thousands of graph indexes, most over a handful of conversations. Project membership compiles into the visibility bitmap instead, which is resolved once per query.

### `Session`

A recorded working period holding several conversations.  A session is a resource rather than a traversal result because it has its own identity, its own span, and its own summaries. "The conversations I had on Tuesday about the merger" is a thing a person names and returns to, and deriving it from edge ordering every time would lose the name.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the session. |
| `display_name` | `string` | 2 | `OPTIONAL` | Human-readable name. |
| `space` | `string` | 3 |  | Space this session belongs to. Mutable, and therefore a field rather than a path segment. |
| `start_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 4 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the working period began. |
| `end_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 5 | `OPTIONAL` | When the working period ended, or unset while it is still open. |
| `conversation_count` | `int32` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Conversations recorded in this session. |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the session was created. |
| `update_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the session was last modified. |
| `delete_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 10 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the session was soft-deleted, or unset while it is live. Present for the same reason it is on every other resource in this tree: `DeleteSession` returns the tombstoned session, and without these there is nowhere for it to say that it is one. A delete that returned a resource indistinguishable from a live one would make `Undelete` unusable — a caller could not tell what needed restoring. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 11 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When a soft-deleted session is purged and becomes unrecoverable. |
| `etag` | `string` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

### `Space`

A named container for related conversation — a finance space, an education space, a private thread with one other person.  A space is the unit at which protection is declared, and that is deliberate rather than incidental: an encrypted space needs its own segments so a whole region decrypts at unlock. Declaring protection per conversation would force per-row decryption and destroy the zero-copy read path.

| Field | Type | # | Behavior | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string` | 1 | `IDENTIFIER` | Resource name of the space. |
| `display_name` | `string` | 2 | `REQUIRED` | Human-readable name, such as `Finance`. |
| `projects` | `repeated string` | 3 |  | Projects this space belongs to. Repeated, and mutable: a space may span projects, and membership is not encoded in the resource name precisely so it can change without renaming anything that refers to this space. |
| `protection` | `Protection` | 4 | `REQUIRED` | How the contents of this space are protected. |
| `locked` | `bool` | 5 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Whether the space is currently readable. A key-wrapped space that has not been unlocked is reported rather than silently skipped: a search that could not read it sets `complete` to false and names it, so a caller can tell "no results" from "no results you can currently see". |
| `create_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 6 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the space was created. |
| `update_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 7 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the space was last modified. |
| `delete_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 8 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When the space was soft-deleted, or unset while it is live. |
| `expire_time` | `google.protobuf.Timestamp` | 9 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | When a soft-deleted space is purged and becomes unrecoverable. |
| `etag` | `string` | 10 | `OUTPUT_ONLY` | Opaque value for optimistic concurrency on update. |

## Enums

### `Protection`

What actually protects the contents of a space.  The distinction is load-bearing rather than descriptive: only the last two involve cryptography, and calling an access-controlled space a vault would invite the assumption that it survives a compromised server.

| Value | # | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `PROTECTION_UNSPECIFIED` | 0 | Default value. Never valid in a request. |
| `PROTECTION_NONE` | 1 | Visible according to ordinary role grants on the containing projects. |
| `PROTECTION_PRIVATE` | 2 | Readable only by its owner, enforced by a visibility predicate. Access control, not cryptography. Anyone who compromises the server reads it, which is exactly why it is not called a vault. |
| `PROTECTION_VAULT` | 3 | Encrypted with a key the server wraps and holds. Contents live in their own segments so unlocking decrypts a region rather than a row at a time. |
| `PROTECTION_SEALED` | 4 | Encrypted with a key only the client holds. The server cannot read the contents even when compromised, and cannot search them while locked. |
